comment: Apache-2.0. Copyright 2026 CYFR Works Inc. Directory HTTP conformance (cyfr-directory/v2), consumed by CYFR and cyfr.run. Each scenario uses a fresh directory, rate windows and settings; omitted settings use production defaults. Requests are literal JSON objects, serialized compactly with UTF-8; null body means no body. The optional source is presented through a trusted proxy, default 198.51.100.1. Query values are strings. A step {"tombstone": identifier} is the operator's tombstone, made through each side's own administrator path (cyfr.run's admin action, a CYFR's directory.tombstone), not over this wire. Expect body fields are a top-level subset with exact nested values; omitted fields are unconstrained, null must be present. Only retry_after uses {min,max}, an inclusive integer range, and a header {body_field:retry_after} must equal that returned integer in decimal. Only listed response headers are constrained: names are case-insensitive, values exact. Content-Type is unconstrained; the response body must still decode as JSON except on a 413. A 413 constrains only status because the endpoint owns its error representation. Entry objects in response entries must also appear as canonical JCS bytes on the wire. keys carries unpadded base64url Ed25519 seeds and public keys, and for alg es256 the P-256 private scalar, uncompressed point and credential id; entries carries pre-signed canonical JCS strings (cyfr-identity/v2), a passkey's made at https://dir.test with relying party dir.test. A write answers 200 with identifier, seq, entry_hash and result (created, exists or accepted), and exists also names the current head; an entry already the one after its prev is exists, a prev that is not the head is stale_head. A malformed entry, a non-genesis at register and a genesis at append are invalid; any other refusal of the chain is unverified with its reason, but duplicate_key, which is 409. Entries signed by a recovery key may spend the recovery reserve; a genesis and an entry a listed key signs may not. Scenarios intentionally omit not_served, read_only and the daily write window, which CYFR tests separately.
